title: Two stars, one temperature: which one is bigger?
subtitle: 3 steps of A Universe of Stars (37 in the full investigation)
body:
Step 1 of 3 predict

Which is bigger, and by how much?

Same two stars. Same surface temperature. One about three hundred times more luminous.

Commit before you measure. The reasoning matters more than the number: a star’s surface area grows as the square of its radius.

💡 Radius, not diameter. Every size in this investigation is a radius, in units of the Sun’s radius — 696,000 km.

title: Two stars, one temperature: which one is bigger?
subtitle: 3 steps of A Universe of Stars (37 in the full investigation)
body:
Step 3 of 3 question

Sideways, at one luminosity

Now move the other way. Put the cursor at 1 solar luminosity and travel along that line, from the cool right-hand side to the hot left-hand side, watching the radius.

At a fixed luminosity, a hotter surface radiates far harder per square meter — as the fourth power of the temperature — so the star needs fewer square meters to put out the same light.

💡 Both moves - up the diagram and along it - are the same relation used in different directions. Nothing new is being introduced.
